content.title: About
content.content: White sauce (béchamel) and gravy are classic culinary foundations used in European and Russian cuisines. Béchamel is made from butter, flour and milk, while gravy may include stock, cream and aromatic additions. Both sauces give dishes a delicate flavor, creamy texture and help bind ingredients together.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Béchamel is one of the five “mother” sauces of French cuisine, based on a roux.
The name “béchamel” comes from Louis de Béchamel, a favorite of King Louis XIV of France.
In Russian cuisine, gravy is often prepared from meat or vegetable stock and thickened with flour or starch.
Cream sauces can be flavored with herbs, cheese, mustard or spices, making them very versatile.
Béchamel is commonly used in lasagna, moussaka, casseroles and as a creamy topping for fish.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Milk in the sauce provides calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk and cream contain vitamin B2 (riboflavin) and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Dairy components add a modest amount of complete protein.

items.title: Improves nutrient absorption
items.content: Fats in cream help absorb fat‑soluble vitamins from other ingredients.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream and milk may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Traditional white sauce contains a lot of saturated fat, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to dairy should avoid the sauce.

items.title: Salt and sodium
items.content: Gravy made from stock can be high in sodium; salt levels should be controlled.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Béchamel works well in casseroles, pasta, vegetable dishes and fish. Gravy is used as a sauce for meat, potatoes, dumplings and in soups. The sauce can be thinned with milk or stock, and flavored with cheese, herbs, or spices to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. When frozen, it may separate; re‑mix thoroughly and gently reheat before use.
